Abstract—This paper investigates grant-free random access
in low Earth orbit satellite Internet-of-Things systems without
global navigation satellite system (GNSS) assistance. To ac-
commodate large differential delays and Doppler shifts across
devices without GNSS-assisted timing and frequency precom-
pensation, we propose a multi-frame afﬁne frequency division
multiplexing (AFDM) transmission scheme and analyze its input-
output relationship. Building on this model, we learn a score-
based generative prior for the AFDM effective channel without
requiring a sparse representation or grid-aligned delay–Doppler
parameters. Training uses colored Gaussian perturbations to
account for correlated estimation errors in the receiver . The
learned prior is then incorporated into a message-passing (MP)
receiver for minimum mean-squared error (MMSE) denoising,
providing posterior mean and variance estimates. These posterior
moments are combined with soft activity probabilities obtained
from a learned density-ratio estimator, thereby incorporating
activity uncertainty into channel estimation. The resulting soft
information is iteratively exchanged with a linear estimation
module for joint activity detection and channel estimation
(JADCE). Numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed
receiver outperforms the baseline receiver in activity detection
and channel estimation.
Index Terms —Afﬁne frequency division multiplexing, grant-
free random access, joint activity detection and channel estima-
tion, score-based generative models.
I. I NTRODUCTION
Sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks are expected to
provide ubiquitous connectivity for a massive number of
Internet-of-Things (IoT) devices [ 1], [ 2]. To serve devices in
remote areas with limited terrestrial coverage, low Earth orbit
(LEO) satellites complement cellular networks for applications
such as smart agriculture and climate monitoring [ 3]. These
power-limited devices transmit short packets sporadically, with
only a small fraction active at a given time [ 1], [ 3]. In grant-
based random access, handshaking before transmission incurs
signiﬁcant signaling overhead, while the long propagation de-
lay of terrestrial-satellite links further increases access latency
[1], [2]. Accordingly, grant-free random access (GFRA) allows
active devices to transmit pilots and data directly without
ﬁrst obtaining a grant, reducing signaling overhead and access
latency in LEO satellite IoT systems [ 1], [ 2].

Supporting GFRA over LEO links requires handling large
delays and Doppler shifts caused by long propagation dis-
tances and high satellite mobility. The 3rd Generation Part-
nership Project (3GPP) Release 17 framework addresses these
effects through device-side pre-compensation assisted by the
global navigation satellite system (GNSS) [ 4]. With such pre-
compensation, many existing satellite GFRA schemes assume
perfect compensation or small residual delays and Doppler
shifts at the receiver [ 3]. However, frequent estimation and
compensation increase energy consumption and reduce battery
lifetime, making these schemes less suitable for power-limited
remote IoT devices [ 3]. This motivates reducing dependence
on GNSS, consistent with the GNSS-independent operation
considered in the Release 19 study on satellite access [ 5].
With reduced reliance on device-side pre-compensation, the
satellite receiver must accommodate large differential delays
and Doppler shifts, which can cause severe inter-symbol and
inter-carrier interference in conventional orthogonal frequency
division multiplexing (OFDM) systems [ 3], [ 6].
To mitigate these effects, orthogonal time frequency space
(OTFS) modulation exploits the quasi-static properties of
channels in the delay–Doppler domain [ 3], [ 7]. In [ 3], multi-
frame OTFS transmission handles large differential delays
and Doppler shifts at the satellite receiver, allowing devices
to operate without GNSS assistance or pre-compensation of
these offsets. However, the two-dimensional transformation
in OTFS entails relatively high modulation complexity [ 6],
[8]. Afﬁne frequency division multiplexing (AFDM), based
on one-dimensional chirp modulation, offers lower modula-
tion complexity than OTFS while retaining strong Doppler
robustness over doubly dispersive channels [ 6], [ 8], [ 9]. With
properly designed chirp parameters, AFDM can also achieve
full diversity over such channels [ 9]. This combination of
low modulation complexity and full diversity makes AFDM
attractive for GFRA with power-limited IoT devices.
To unleash the full potential of AFDM-GFRA, accurate joint
activity detection and channel estimation (JADCE) is a critical
prerequisite [ 8]. Existing methods exploit sporadic device
activity to formulate JADCE as a compressed sensing (CS)
problem and incorporate structured priors to capture channel
sparsity [3], [8]. The scheme in [ 8] further uses a graph neural
network to adaptively learn sparsity patterns, while retaining
a predeﬁned delay–Doppler grid for the sparse channel rep-
resentation. However, in practical propagation environments,
fractional Doppler shifts and fractional time delays can intro-

duce signiﬁcant power leakage in the effective channel matrix,
thereby weakening its sparsity [ 6]. This motivates learning
effective-channel priors from data to capture channel structures
beyond the assumed sparse representation [ 1], [ 6].
Score-based generative models learn channel priors from
samples by estimating the score function of the channel dis-
tribution [ 10], [ 11]. In [ 6], score-based learning is performed
directly on the AFDM effective channel to address fractional
delay–Doppler off-grid leakage in channel estimation. For
massive random access, [ 12] proposes a two-stage algorithm
that ﬁrst identiﬁes active users through a Transformer-based
detector and then uses generative diffusion models for joint
channel estimation and data detection. However, both ap-
proaches rely on iterative posterior sampling, which requires
repeated score function evaluations and incurs substantial
computational cost [ 6], [ 12].
To avoid iterative posterior sampling, [ 1] develops a score-
based turbo message passing (STMP) algorithm that incorpo-
rates generative channel priors for JADCE. Through Tweedie’s
formulas, separate ﬁrst- and second-order score networks
provide posterior means and variances for single-step min-
imum mean-squared error (MMSE) denoising under equiv-
alent additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) observations.
However, this AWGN model is justiﬁed in the large-system
limit with right-rotationally invariant random sensing matrices
[1]. In the ﬁnite-dimensional, structured multi-frame AFDM
system considered here, departures from these conditions can
exacerbate the mismatch between denoiser input errors and
the white Gaussian perturbations used for training. A similar
limitation has been highlighted for structured compression
matrices in [13]. This mismatch can degrade channel denoising
accuracy and, consequently, JADCE performance. Moreover,
[1] computes activity probabilities using Gaussian extrinsic
messages obtained after projecting the channel posterior onto
a Gaussian distribution. In general, matching posterior means
and variances does not preserve the marginal likelihood as-
sociated with a non-Gaussian channel prior. Consequently,
the resulting likelihood ratio can yield inaccurate activity
probabilities even when the channel posterior moments are
accurately estimated. These errors further affect the activity-
weighted channel estimates exchanged with the linear estima-
tion module.
Against this background, we investigate GNSS-independent
AFDM-GFRA for LEO satellite IoT systems. Our main con-
tributions are summarized as follows:
1) We develop a multi-frame AFDM transmission scheme
that handles large differential delays and Doppler shifts
at the satellite receiver. The derived input–output re-
lationship retains fractional delay–Doppler effects and
the chirp-periodic preﬁx phase for delays exceeding the
useful symbol duration. Separating the phase evolution
across frames yields a multiple measurement vector
(MMV) model in which the effective channel of each
device remains approximately constant over consecutive
frames. Additional pilot frames therefore provide more
observations without increasing the number of channel
coefﬁcients to be estimated.
2) We learn a score-based generative prior directly from
multiantenna AFDM effective-channel samples with frac-
tional delays and Doppler shifts. The denoiser is trained
with colored Gaussian perturbations and conditioned on
their covariance to account for correlations in the denoiser
input error.
3) We develop a message-passing JADCE receiver for the
structured multi-frame AFDM observation model. A
learned density-ratio estimator compares the active and
inactive observation distributions under the effective-
channel prior to obtain soft activity probabilities. These
probabilities are combined with channel posterior mean
and variance estimates obtained using the learned prior to
form Gaussian extrinsic messages for iterative exchange
with the linear estimation module. Simulation results
demonstrate that the proposed receiver improves activity
detection and channel estimation performance compared
with STMP across different signal-to-noise ratios and
pilot-frame counts.
